episodes.194700: A long tracked thunderstorm developed over Phillips County and moved east across northeast Montana, reaching severe intensity at times.
episodes.194728: A warm front approaching central Pennsylvania in an environment of sufficient instability and shear allowed for thunderstorm formation during the late afternoon and evening hours, with multiple rounds of severe thunderstorms crossing the northern tier of Pennsylvania. The multiple rounds of heavy rainfall, coupled with local topography, allowed for flash flooding across hydrologically sensitive areas of Potter and Tioga counties. As thunderstorms progressed southward into the Lower Susquehanna Valley, they began to congeal into a line of thunderstorms producing more widespread wind damage.
episodes.194744: Despite abnormally dry to drought conditions across central Indiana, following two weeks with no rain for most locations; dewpoints climbing to around 70 degrees on the 20th promoted scattered evening showers and thunderstorms with embedded isolated microbursts.||Synoptically, the broad subtropical upper ridge which had been suppressed south for much of the month, returned northward into the Midwest, with moderate south-southwesterly breezes increasing humidity and precipitable water values.  A boundary slowly crossing northwestern Indiana initiated convection.  Showers and storms with locally heavy downpours crossed the region, with damaging micobursts from the two strongest cells:  first late-day in south-central Howard County, and then later in the evening over south-central Marion County.
episodes.194792: An upper level low from the Pacific approached New Mexico from the west bringing southwesterly flow aloft, overriding moist surface conditions across the eastern plains of New Mexico. It was a classic severe weather scenario with discrete super cells developing over portions of the eastern plains and northern mountains of New Mexico. Severe hail was reported near Espanola, Clovis and north of Roswell. Flash flooding was also reported within the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar in Mora County.
episodes.195044: A strong upper level low pressure system moving across the southwestern United States into the four-corners region brought ample lift to create scattered thunderstorms late in the afternoon of the 21st. Thunderstorms initially developed across eastern New Mexico by mid-afternoon in response to the approaching upper level system and moderate boundary layer instability. These thunderstorms moved into the extreme southwestern Texas Panhandle late in the afternoon producing large hail up to two inches in diameter and several severe wind gusts. Hail up to two inches in diameter in Dimmitt destroyed numerous car windshields. Several gustnadoes were observed along the leading edge of activity as it tracked across the area. Increasing low level shear, due to a low level jet, interacted with the inflow to a thunderstorm east of Dimmitt (Castro County) producing a brief tornado in an open field. Although storms were moving quickly during the late afternoon through early evening, repeated rounds of storms created flash flooding in and around Dimmitt and flooding in isolated other locations.
episodes.195126: A small cluster of thunderstorms developed in response to a strong low-level jet, MUCAPE up to 1000 J/kg, and effective shear of 35-40 knots. A brief stronger updraft produced up to ping-pong ball size hail around Marshall.
episodes.195291: A weak shortwave trough produced isolated convection along a northeastward moving surface cold front. There were a few reports of marginally severe hail and wind during the morning in portions of west and east central Minnesota.
episodes.195292: A weak shortwave trough produced isolated convection along a northeastward moving surface cold front. There was one report of marginally severe hail and one report of sub-severe hail during the morning in portions of western Wisconsin.
episodes.195326: A few pulse severe thunderstorms developed on the evening of September 21st. These thunderstorms produced downburst winds and large hail just to the southwest of Springfield.
episodes.195398: A few severe thunderstorms produced isolated hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195512: As an upper-level shortwave trough traversed west to east across the northern Great Plains, a surface cold front pushed southeast into the central Plains and the Omaha NWS County Warning Area. During the afternoon hours, scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed along and ahead of this front, bringing multiple reports of quarter sized hails and wind gusts up to 63 miles per hour to locations in southeast Nebraska.
episodes.195606: A cold front advanced eastward from the Great Lakes into the area, and provided a lifting mechanism for convective development during the afternoon and evening hours of September 21. Despite only modest instability and limited shear, though with additional support from an upper level jet streak, multicellular and lines of storms were still able to develop, mainly along the Blue Ridge before tracking east. Some of these storms were severe across the Piedmont and Foothills of Virginia, with many reports of wind damage in this region.
episodes.195661: A strong disturbance dropped out of southern Ontario and across Central New York triggering the development of scattered showers and a few thunderstorms, mainly west of I-81. A couple of storms over Steuben County became strong to severe with reports of downed trees occurring on a couple of roads over central portions of the county.
episodes.195782: Scattered thunderstorms developed ahead of a warm front during the late afternoon and tracked through central Wisconsin through the early evening hours on Saturday (9/21).  The strongest storms produced hail up to penny size.
episodes.195799: Outflow dominant area of scattered thunderstorms moved northeast across central and east-central Kansas, producing scattered severe wind gusts and wind damage.
episodes.195964: Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms moved through the combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles as well as eastern New Mexico and parts of West Texas throughout the day on the 21st. Some clearing in the clouds during the late morning and early afternoon helped parts of the southern Texas Panhandle warm up. This warming helped to destabilize the atmosphere and lead to an afternoon/evening round of storms become severe.
episodes.196064: As a surface low pressure system moved across northern Kansas, a southwest to northeast cold front descended into Kansas initiating multiple storm systems with ample low-level moisture.
episodes.196139: Throughout much of the day on September 21st, an outflow boundary moved from north to south through the region. As this occurred, storms developed along this boundary and produced large hail and wind damage from the late morning until the evening hours.
episodes.196140: During the late afternoon hours on September 21st, an outflow boundary helped develop a supercell thunderstorm in Fillmore County. Soon after it developed it dropped golf ball sized hail two miles east of Whalan.
episodes.196142: During the late afternoon on September 21st, a supercell thunderstorm briefly passed through northeastern Allamakee County. As the storm moved through it produced small hail and some minor tree damage.
episodes.196339: A thunderstorm with strong outflow moved into Butler County and caused damage to outbuildings near Burns. There was damage to a machine shed which was moved off the foundation. Another outbuilding lost part of its metal roof.
episodes.196395: Upper-level ridging peaked over the forecast area on the 21st. Scattered storms developed in the northeastern part of the Quad State closer to the warm front near a residual boundary. CAPE values near 2000 J/kg and DCAPE values near 1000 J/kg allowed for downdraft development. Effective bulk shear of 25 kts was sufficient for storms, but somewhat limited. Tree damage was observed in White County just west of the bridge over the Wabash River.
episodes.196422: Air traffic control reported a funnel cloud to the east of the tower.
episodes.196433: A thunderstorm developed and became severe over eastern Montana and then moved into northwestern North Dakota. As the thunderstorm passed over the Williston Airport, it produced wind gusts of 61 mph.
episodes.196485: A mid-level shortwave and upper jet support promoted the development of scattered thunderstorms across portions of far southern Pennsylvania and northern West Virginia during the early to middle afternoon hours of September 21st. Deep-layer shear supported storm organization and rotation, leading to several instances of damaging wind, and a couple isolated reports of large hail.
episodes.196486: A mid-level shortwave and upper jet support promoted the development of scattered thunderstorms across portions of far southern Pennsylvania and northern West Virginia during the early to middle afternoon hours of September 21st. Deep-layer shear supported storm organization and rotation, leading to several instances of damaging wind, and a couple isolated reports of large hail.
episodes.196498: Showers moved into the western New York area on the afternoon of Saturday September 21st. With shortwave trough over the area and within a northwest flow regime, along with around 1,500 J/kg of surface based CAPE thunderstorms developed within the showers. With conditions mostly favorable, thunderstorms became strong to severe at times during the afternoon. The thunderstorms caused damaging wind gusts and large hail to the size of golf balls. Heavy rainfall associated with the thunderstorms caused Flash Flooding in several areas across Allegany County. Thunderstorm wind damage was limited to only two counties, Allegany and Wyoming.
episodes.196518: Scattered evening (on the 20th) convection across the southern High Plains congealed into a loosely organized convective system during the early morning of the 21st. This system produced a severe-caliber wind gust near the Oklahoma/Kansas border.
episodes.196617: A cold front trekking through the Ohio Valley on September 21st resulted in two instances of strong thunderstorms across West Virginia. The first storm that entered into Tyler County on that afternoon resulted in damaging winds as the direct result of a microburst. This contributed to significant roof and tree damage along a street within the town of Sistersville. Another storm toppled down a single tree in Lewis County. Otherwise, radar activity proved to be weak and did not cause any other storm damage in the state. An excessive amount of moisture accompanying the front also yielded bursts of heavy rainfall. A member of the public recorded 1.45 inches of rain had fallen at their home near Hacker Valley in Webster County. However, with the historic drought ongoing in West Virginia, the ground was able to soak up the rain and did not lead to any reports of flash flooding.
episodes.196637: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed along and north of a warm front during the afternoon and evening hours of September 21. Storms produced sporadic reports of wind damage and large hail in Dane and Iowa Counties.
episodes.196664: The proximity of an upper level trough, along with an area of enhanced moisture, very light winds and strong heating resulted in explosive convection developing over Puerto Rico. The thunderstorms produced very heavy rainfall, lightning, gusty winds, and even hail. Flooding and landslides were reported in several areas in Puerto Rico. Water surges along rivers were common, with some rivers even reaching flood stage.
episodes.196784: An upper level low moved across Arizona during the night with showers and thunderstorms.  One storm produce severe hail.
episodes.196951: Numerous thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours of September 20th and quickly became severe as they entered into portions of central and south-central Kansas. Storms progressed eastward then produced up to quarter-sized hail and damaging wind gusts between 60 and 70 mph. However, some storms across south-central Kansas later into the evening and nighttime hours produced significant damage with wind gusts estimated to be up around 90 mph. Damage produced by these storms included high-profile vehicles and semis being blown over, a plethora of power poles and trees either damaged or snapped, and significant damage to a large outbuilding.
